hosts.scope: C, Rust and fwp count decimal characters for i and checked 3*i over 0 <= i < 2000000, with checked accumulation and output 28518516. Saved C/Rust and fwp executables come from the audited earlier run. Matched C/Rust use the candidate algorithm from the measurement source, with GCC O2 and Rust -O respectively. Compare these peers to assess remaining overhead; comparison with old peers also changes algorithms. All matched helpers carry ordinary inline hints, not forced inlining. Grouped-unhinted removes only the two fwp inline hints to isolate their cost. Recomputed-product keeps the same signed overflow check and expresses the product again on its non-overflow continuation. This comparison rewrites saved generated C. The workflow separately verifies actual compiler-produced C and its executable; measurements alone do not establish full arithmetic acceptance. GCC range and optimized tree dumps accompany each C rebuild. Rebuilt fwp uses unchanged saved C; candidate changes only integer digit counting to descending decimal groups. Both use GCC O2, no LTO. Balanced whole-process timing includes startup, output and shutdown; wall time includes Python subprocess launch, child CPU excludes parent and descheduling. Compilation, audit and memory instrumentation are outside timing. Each allowed CPU is pinned separately. ASLR is recorded and unchanged. Every sample is retained. Separate instrumented binaries measure managed storage after constant initialization, excluding raw buffers, libc, stacks and metadata. These measurements do not prove causality for historical variability.
